why: pushCompletionsBatch chunks at _writeBatchLimit=500 and, per the documented H3 fix, must report only the entityKeys of chunks that actually committed when a later chunk throws, so OutboxProcessor deletes exactly the landed rows and retries the rest. Group 5's largest test pushes only 10 items — never crosses a chunk boundary — and group 15's 'SyncPushException partial-commit reporting' test just constructs a SyncPushException object directly and checks its own constructor round-trips fields; it never calls pushCompletionsBatch at all. A regression in the chunk loop (e.g. moving pushed.addAll before batch.commit(), or an off-by-one in the start/end clamp) would re-push or silently drop already-committed outbox rows and this suite would not notice.
recommendation: Add a test that pushes >500 items where a wrapped/stubbed Firestore batch throws on the second chunk, and assert pushCompletionsBatch throws SyncPushException with committed containing exactly chunk 1's entityKeys and none of chunk 2's.
acceptance_criteria: New test drives >500 items through the real pushCompletionsBatch code path (not a hand-constructed exception) with an injected failure on chunk 2 and asserts SyncPushException.committed equals exactly chunk 1's keys
Test fails red if the chunk loop's addAll/commit ordering is swapped
